Services,

Bangladesh is highly vulnerable to climate change because of its low-lying deltaic geography, extensive rivers, dense population, coastal exposure, and dependence on climate-sensitive livelihoods. Despite these challenges, Bangladesh has demonstrated strong commitment to climate action through adaptation, mitigation, disaster risk reduction, community-based initiatives, institutional development, and international cooperation.

The Department of Environment (DoE), under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, plans to produce a high-quality 8-10 minutes video documentary, along with a shorter 4-5 minutes version highlighting Bangladesh's climate vulnerability, impacts, government and community responses, key achievements, and vision for a climate-resilient and low-emission future.

The documentary will serve as a strategic communication and advocacy tool for COPs, UNFCCC meetings, international conferences, seminars, workshops, climate exhibitions, donor events, bilateral and multilateral meetings, and other national and international platforms.
